reviews.snippet:
I have gone to Manipal hospital with a knee twisting injury. From MRI report I got to know the ACL ligament was torn apart. The only of  correction was via surgery. But I couldn't go for thr surgery just yet because my knee was sort of locked and I had excruciating pain in my knee.

I met Jonathan sir for physiotherapy. He explained me the entire pre and post rehab program. With no time my knee pain started to settle down and I got my knee flexibility back.Post that I underwent surgery by Dr ayyapan and after that again started with post surgery rehab under Jonathan.Its been 3 weeks post surgery I am getting my strenght back and am able to walk with a stick.

Fart forward 2025, I had come for my mother’s consultancy; got her registered and showed to the doctor. Doctor asked to do reports, I came back to show the reports to the doctor; they have charged me the full consultation charge. This is not done at all. I didn’t even bring the patient with me, just for the reports charging full fees is robbery!

reviews.snippet:
I had come to the hospital with complain of knee pain and hand pain. I waited patiently in the emergency ward while the doctor came to examine. After the doctor examination, she advised to go to OPD. There was no staff available with wheelchair. I waited for ten minutes and then walked on my own to the OPD. There as well had to wait for registration and billing. The doctor was so concerned about his own safety that he didnt examine my knee and for my hand, he used a paper to hold it. He sent me for xray and told to come quickly as he has to leave early. Again i asked for wheelchair and again nobody brought it. I walked and went and paid for xray and was told  to wait for an hour.
I am not sure what to understand about this hospital. I was told it is superb and excellent hospital but a hospital which cannot provide a basic wheelchair for patient cannot be excellent hospital. Hospital where patient has to hear from doctor that get xray fast as i have to leave early cannot be excellent hospital. A hospital where patient is limping and walking and literally nobody gives damn cannot be excellent hospital. If you are sure that you do not have sufficient staff to run hospital smoothly then either hire people or don't open hospital. You cannot open hospital and charge patients and not provide basic care.

reviews.snippet:
We booked an appointment to show my wife for knee problem to Dr Juneja on 17 Aug 21. Appointment was given for 17.45 we reached well in time at 17.30 but doctor was not to be seen till 18.00.
We waited, Waited and waited and found the doctor with a patient. I had to barge in to ask if we would be seen today or we have to come again. Doctor checked on computer and said " I am not aware that you are waiting" . He still took another 30 minutes to call us and advised an X Ray. We reached x ray department to wait for the technician. With great difficulty, and intervention of a supervisor could get the X Ray done. Came back to Dr Juneja with X Ray and again wait, wait and wait. He was again found with new consultation patients and just not bothered to see the patients who with X Rays. We got so cheesed off that after waiting for another one hour, we informed the supervisor and left the hospital under protest.
This has been our worst experience at Manipal hospital Whitefield Bangalore.

reviews.snippet:
Last year we had to get two surgeries done at Manipal Whitefield and the experience over-all was that of knowing that my family would be looked after. Dr. Kumardev who performed knee surgery for my spouse and Dr. Anoop T. who created a fistula (required for dialysis) for my father were both excellent, not just during consultation and the procedure, but also during pre and post-patient care. I would highly recommend them both, anytime! We also consulted Dr. Ravi Shankar (Nephrologist) and were quite satisfied (read: at peace) with his advise - it was practical and honest.
Yes, there was the usual long-waits, follow-up with the nurses to ensure medication was administered on time and a few disagreements, but the care received from the respective doctors was something that I can swear by. Also, funny as it may sound, if I am being charged for a bottle of sanitiser, ideally that's mine! Maybe a little bit more transparency is required at the administration level. Secondly, the pharmacy definitely needs to be better stocked! They inadvertently are 'out of stock' of even the most basic medicines.
